projects.title: Show HN: Live audio dubbing from any browser tab
projects.author: christiansafka
projects.summary: Hey HN, at Pinch we've been working on something to reduce friction to getting accurate, fast audio translation for live media. Initially we launched a desktop app that sat between your hardware mic/speakers and your meeting platform, but this required users to install our audio driver which introduced permissions hoops to jump through as well as stability issues across updates, not to mention trying to get our device driver approved by Microsoft.. So today we're launching Pinch Sidecar, which offers speech to speech translation in-browser for any Chrome browser tab. This is accomplished by sharing the tab audio with our page, where we proceed to mute the original tab and mix in our translated audio with speaker-matched voices. We also offer meeting creators using Google Meet, Zoom, or Teams the ability to host a translated meeting where listeners can listen and interact in their own language through our Sidecar. The tab translation mode is open for free testing for this HN launch. Our ask is just to let us know how it goes, and to share the link to anyone you know organizing multilingual webinars/meetings.

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一个我做的开源桌面工具 Kiri，支持 macOS 和 Windows。 写文档或反馈问题时，经常需要截张图、画个箭头，或者录一段操作过程。Kiri 把这些操作放在同一个快捷入口里：选中窗口或区域后，可以截图、标注、识别文字或录屏。 主要功能 截图与标注：截取窗口或区域，添加箭头、文字、马赛克等标注，保存后还能继续编辑。 本地 OCR：使用系统自带的文字识别，不需要配置 API Key。识别结果和原图一起保留，之后可以按关键词搜索、复制和回看。 区域录屏：输出 MP4 或 GIF，可选系统声音和鼠标点击高亮，适合演示操作或反馈问题。 截图、录像和文字记录统一保存在本地素材库，支持收藏、标签和搜索。截图、OCR 和视频编码默认都在本机完成。 演示视频 观看界面操作演示（MP4） 视频展示截图标注、文字识别界面、录屏和素材库的操作流程；捕获和 OCR 使用示例数据，详见录制说明。 项目采用 MIT 协议开源，欢迎试用和反馈。 项目源码 · 下载安装

projects.title: DrawDog
projects.summary: Clients are starting to ask freelancers to prove their work wasn't generated. DrawDog sits in your menu bar and records how your file grew, what apps were in front of you, and whether an AI tool was ever open. It signs and timestamps that record, then gives you one link to send. The client drags your file onto the page to confirm it's the one you certified. It never looks inside your work: no screen recording, no keystrokes, no file names. Three certificates a month, free.

projects.title: Show HN: Rdltr – Inbox zero for your reading list
projects.author: eduardosasso
projects.summary: Hi HN, for the past few months I’ve been working on a read later app called RDLTR ( https://rdltr.app ). The whole thing started because I had so many tabs open with stuff I wanted to read, across browsers, Mac, Linux, and iPhone. They cluttered everything and got in the way of other things I had to do. Pocket had just shut down when this idea came up, I looked around, tried Instapaper, Raindrop, Matter, and a few others I forget. They were fine, but they all give you a list that only grows, which is another thing to maintain, and not the model I had in mind. Safari has this Reading List feature where you read something and it drops off the unread list. But it’s Apple only and half worked. What I wanted was inbox zero for reading. Open something, read it, come back, and it’s gone from the queue but still in the archive. You keep going until there is nothing left. Links come in from anywhere. Paste a URL on the page, drag one in, or use the bookmarklet, the Chrome and Firefox extensions, or the Apple Shortcut for the iOS share sheet, plus Vim keys, TL;DR summaries on each link, search across everything you have read or saved, RSS for every list, and it works just as well on the phone. The extensions have a couple of tricks that I use all the time. Shift+DD pulls the article text, cleans it up, and sends it to ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini in a new tab, so you can ask it anything about what you just read. Shift+AA opens it in the Internet Archive, handy for paywalled sites when you don’t have a subscription. The stack is Bun, TypeScript, HTMX, and SQLite, with SSE so the list updates the moment you save or read something, deployed on a Hetzner VPS. Full disclosure, Claude Code wrote most of it. I still spent a ton of time dogfooding, testing, and polishing the UI until things felt right. Anyway, curious to know what your current setup is for this.

projects.title: Revindo

You type a plain instruction and the agent drafts the listing, suggests a price anchored on real completed sales rather than the last displayed price, prepares buyer replies, and surfaces underpriced items to resell. No cloud bot touches your account, and a STOP button stays visible. Vinted in production; Leboncoin under construction.

Recordings can become AI reports with transcripts, interactions, and keyframes. Annotate screenshots, keep clipboard history, and share video demos by link. Free during public beta. macOS 14+.

projects.title: Vibe Eyes
projects.summary: I miss my dog when I am at my desk all day. So now he lives in my menu bar. Drop in a photo and Vibe Eyes turns your own pet into a tiny animated avatar up there. It follows your cursor, blinks at you, winks when you click and looks up when you have been away. Small stuff, but you catch yourself glancing up and smiling. Eleven pets built in, free. projects.title: mactap
projects.summary: MacTap is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that turns knocks on your MacBook chassis into shortcuts. One, two, or three knocks copy, paste, accept an AI suggestion, take a screenshot, control media, or anything you map. It reads the accelerometer inside the unibody (the same sensor that detects if your laptop is falling) and classifies knocks on-device. Nothing gets uploaded, no account, no network calls. Just a small native Swift app sitting in your menu bar.

projects.title: Flash Mask
projects.author: sudohg
projects.summary: Flash Mask 是一款帮助你在与 AI 或 Agent 协作时，清楚说明图片中哪个位置需要修改的辅助工具。当你需要让 AI 修改图片中的某个局部区域时，只需拖入图片，圈出一处或多处区域，即可快速生成记录圈选位置和修改要求的 JSON 数据，省去在大型图像软件中反复框选、导出的繁琐步骤。 典型使用场景包括：当你只想让 AI 修改图片中的某个细节时，圈出需要处理的区域，例如角色图中的手、脸或配件，照片背景里的路人或杂物，海报中的局部元素；也可以为 Coding Agent 标记 UI 截图中的问题位置，如 iOS Simulator、原生 App、Canvas、WebGL、地图、图表或游戏 UI 中的文字截断、控件重叠和布局错位。一次可标记多个区域，并将位置与修改要求一起交给 Agent。 主要功能： • 快速标记区域：拖入图片后直接圈选一处或多处需要修改的区域，并可附加文字说明。 • 一键复制 JSON：默认将包含图片路径和尺寸、区域坐标及可选修改要求的 JSON 数据复制到剪贴板，可直接粘贴给正在使用的 Agent，无需先导出蒙版。 • 导出黑白蒙版：需要更精细的处理时，可导出与原图尺寸一致的黑白蒙版。白色表示圈选区域，黑色表示其他区域。 • 支持的图片格式：PNG、JPEG/JPG、WebP。 Flash Mask 负责生成位置数据和蒙版，实际的图片修改由你使用的 AI 或 Agent 完成。 所有图片和蒙版均在本机处理，可离线使用，无需账户。

projects.title: Gojo
projects.summary: Gojo puts local dictation, clipboard history, window controls, a file shelf, and media controls in your MacBook notch. Download a speech model, then dictate into the field you're using. Recognition runs on your Mac in local mode. Includes calendar, battery, camera, and display controls. macOS 14+. Three-day trial; monthly and one-time licenses.

projects.title: CutX

Press ⌘X on a file or folder, then ⌘V where you want it. The items move. CutX never touches your files — it asks Finder to do the move, so undo, progress, Replace/Keep Both and permission prompts all work as usual. Outside Finder, ⌘X still cuts text. Free, open source, no tracking. 11 languages, incl. mirrored Arabic.

Drop it on Rename, Summarize, Extract Text, Transcribe, or Explain and the result lands next to the original, with Undo in the menu bar. Everything runs on-device with Apple's models in macOS 26: no account, no upload, no telemetry. Needs no Accessibility permission. 25 free actions, then a one-time purchase.

projects.title: FlokinMD

projects.title: ClickScrape
projects.summary: ClickScrape is a Chrome extension for pulling structured data off a webpage without writing code or paying a monthly scraping subscription. Click the fields you want on the page. ClickScrape collects them from every matching item, follows pagination and infinite scroll as you browse, and can follow each item's link for detail-page fields. Export to Excel, CSV or JSON, copy to clipboard, or download images as a ZIP. $5.99 one-time, no subscription. Runs locally in your browser.

projects.title: Ergoblin
projects.summary: You call this a hunt? Your ancestors ran antelope to death over 2 days to survive. You've been slouching in that chair scrolling product launches while your eyes dry up into raisins. I see where we are. I'm a mouthy goblin who lives in your menu bar who asks for basic human functions your body is begging for. There are 7 kinds of neglect on my list and you're doing at least 4 right now. I have moods. Put me off and I get less polite. Tell me you can't and I make the ask smaller. Mac and Windows.

projects.title: Verdant

Verdant features an ink-and-paper aesthetic and a local-first architecture — your data never leaves your machine. Use our BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) model to connect OpenAI or Anthropic at raw API cost, or hook up a local model for 100% private, air-gapped synthesis. Available for Mac, Windows, and Linux.

projects.title: Show HN: Browser only CSV editor, data never leaves your machine
projects.author: anshulsahni
projects.summary: The current software I am working upon as part of my full time job, I have to deal with very long JSONs and lot of CSVs. For editing or viewing JSONs my first and obivous choice was jsonher.io, it’s the most wonderful JSON viewer I have ever seen. But I wish I could the same for CSVs too, when I googled it, I couldn’t find anything good. Most of the tools were asking me to sign up, some of them allowed me to open CSV but then came a big popup asking for my credit card so that I can edit it or use some filters, and lot of them were sending CSV to server in case it was large. I will be honest, there were some which were no signup or no server, but their UX was bad - sublime was showing the content better than those. Then I started building one for myself, and it turns out building no signup, browser only CSV tool is actually possible even for managing large CSVs; I was able to make it up and running within days and it turns out to be awesome - apologies for shameless bragging. Later I added support for downloading content in JSON and other alternatives of CSV like PSV, TSV, SSV, etc. It has all the basic functionalities for working with CSVs - filtering, sorting, editing, deleting, downloading in your desired format. In near future, I am planning to make it one shot CSV editor for all kinds of platform - browser extensions, desktop app and hopefully mobile apps too ( I am bad at building mobile apps, but I will try my best ). Do check it out and let me know in comments, what you feel about it.

Keep photos and videos in separate iPhone spaces with album passcodes, Face ID or Touch ID, decoy content, and face-down quick hide. projects.title: Show HN: Gote – a CLI note-taking management tool for plain Markdown
projects.author: banorton
projects.summary: Repo: https://github.com/banorton/gote I built a note taking management tool to use at work for quick note taking and searching. It is intended to be quite minimal. Another focus was to have lots of shortcuts and to keep things close to the homerow for ergonomics and speed. Notes are just markdown files in whatever directory you point it at. The only thing it keeps elsewhere is an index in ~/.gote. If you stop using it you still have all your notes. Tags go on the first line of the note, separated by periods, like .project.urgent.work. No frontmatter. Search is built into the binary, BM25 with stemming, so there's no ripgrep or fzf to set up. gote s meeting searches titles and content, gote s -t .work filters by tag, gote s -w 2412 pulls up notes from December 2024. Most commands have a two letter version that combines a list with an action. ro is recent + open, sv is search + view, tp is tag + pin. When results come up you pick one with a home row key instead of arrows or numbers. Binaries for mac/linux/windows are on the releases page, or go install github.com/banorton/gote@latest if you have Go. The goal of this project was not to learn something new or build something impressive. I simply had a need and filled it with a vibe-coded solution. I have been using it for about a year now and it does more or less exactly what I wanted. So I thought I'd share in case others are interested in using it, contributing to it, or want to use it as a reference for their own solution.

projects.title: AI Chat Exporter
projects.summary: AI Chat Exporter is a free, open-source browser extension for taking your AI conversations with you. Export chats from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Qwen, Meta AI and more to Markdown, JSON, HTML, PDF, Word or PNG. Everything is processed locally in your browser. No accounts, no cloud processing, and no chat data sent to third-party servers. It also supports clipboard rich-text copying, chat continuation between AI platforms, custom filenames and a browser side panel.

projects.title: kiddyproof
projects.summary: one shortcut and your Mac's keyboard and trackpad stop reaching any app, but the screen stays looking exactly how you left it (Slack open, half-typed message and all). your kid can go ham on the keys and none of it lands, they just get calm glowing light to poke at. exit is a deliberate 3-second parent hold. signed and notarized, no account, no cloud.

projects.title: Lyrimuse
projects.summary: Word-synced desktop lyrics for Apple Music, Spotify, QQ Music, NetEase, Kugou, and for YouTube Music or Spotify Web in a browser. Nine lyric providers are queried at once and every candidate is scored on one scale — title, artist, album, duration fit, word-level timing — so live takes, Cantonese versions and radio edits get the words that actually match. Shows up as a floating overlay, a Dynamic Island capsule, an Apple-Music-style window, or in the menu bar. Free and open source, no account.

projects.title: Notchful
projects.summary: You already spend your day at the desk. That's where the water should get logged. Notchful lives in your MacBook notch. Hover to see today's progress. Click once to log a drink. Keep working. Nothing to open. Nothing to unlock. By the time you close your laptop, you've already hit your hydration goal without thinking about it. History by week, month, and year. Goal and cup size in Settings. Everything else from the menu bar.

projects.title: AppGacha
projects.summary: AppGacha turns a plain-language wish into a real desktop app—utilities, widgets, games, and personal tools. Apps run locally, stay portable, and can be organized into your own desktop workspace.

projects.title: MenuBar Notes
projects.summary: Capture a thought without leaving what you’re doing. MenuBar Notes is a compact, Mac-native notes app built for quick capture, focused writing and privacy.

projects.title: WordSmart – Automatic Word Formatting
projects.summary: WordSmart is an early Windows desktop tool that automates repetitive Microsoft Word formatting. It helps format headings, paragraphs, tables, fonts, spacing, and alignment while keeping documents consistent. It also supports large documents and ready-made formatting templates. We’re launching this early MVP to learn from real users, understand their Word workflows, and decide which formatting problems and features to focus on next.

projects.title: Slit — make your Mac unstoppable
projects.summary: Slit is a macOS menu bar app that watches memory pressure, quits idle apps, cleans junk, and finds duplicate files. Free to monitor. One purchase to clean.

projects.title: Liang
projects.summary: Liang is a small macOS menu bar app that shows your AI coding agent's state on your screen, no more switching back to check. A soft glow around the notch, a glow following your cursor, and a menu bar icon show whether your agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy) is thinking, waiting, or done. Each state has its own color. It uses each IDE's official hooks and is local-first: no account, no telemetry, no cloud, and never reads your code or prompts. macOS 14+ and Apple Silicon only.

projects.title: Pastea
projects.summary: Pastea is a clipboard history manager for macOS. It saves every link, snippet and screenshot you copy, so you can search, pin and paste it back in seconds.

projects.title: Show HN: Flying Letters and a Clean Keyboard That Even Steve Jobs Would Like
projects.author: vitalipom
projects.summary: Everyone talks about the negative impact of the screens, but have you been wondering recently around, imagining you’re typing something with some imaginary keyboard? Keyboards differ, some have more memojies, some ultra-high-4k-super-dooper keyboards like Samsung’s app store’s Cafe Keyboard have even plenty of effects. But there is one keyboard, very well hidden, called Effectedkeyboard2 which is not just neatly designed, but also has a feature non of the other keyboards has - flying letters, like in Harry Potter movies, that in addition to all other effects this keyboard offers, this particular effect flies letters as you type - with animation, into your screen! If you happened to stop to try it out, check out some another amazing features that it has: such as more convenient typing caret mover. Long press spacebar till it turns blue and voila, you can drag your fingers through the regular keys to move typing caret even after the phone restarts! Very handy in long text editing. Or else undo/redo options. Have you deleted something useful? Just like in Anysoftkeyboard, which this keyboard is originally based on, swipe up from the spacebar and there you have undo/redo options and on a long press on the paste icon even a clipboard. Unlike Anysoftkeyboard however, Effectedkeyboard2 refreshes its emojies with modern shiny emojies. It has additional visual effects as you type - which mostly cost a couple of dollars, but each is available for a preview under Effects menu in the main settings. Effectedkeyboard2 has been crafted by its developer Vitali Pom. Over the course of 15 years and is now waiting for you to try it out. https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.vitali.pom... Got any questions? Let me know what you think here in the comments.

projects.title: Viewlyt Studio
projects.summary: Jahaan har pal ek yaad ban jaaye. - ViewLyt The simple way for photographers to deliver event photos. Send a private gallery your clients pick from on their phone, or put a QR at the event so guests scan a selfie and get every photo of themselves. Free desktop app — your clients get a free app too.

projects.title: Flick for Mac
projects.summary: Flick is a radial command wheel for macOS. Hold a key, flick your mouse toward an action, release. Launch apps, snap windows, take screenshots, run scripts and Shortcuts, paste clipboard text, control media: one gesture for all of it. Free tier: one wheel of 8 slots, 7 action categories, no account, no time limit. Pro is $19.99 once for up to 5 Macs, with a 30-day free trial.

projects.title: StandBye
projects.summary: StandBye is a bring-your-own-keys Desktop app. Describe a team of AI agents and they keep working on your repo around the clock: they check in, talk in channels, ask you only when a decision is yours, and remember what they learn.

projects.title: LUFScale
projects.summary: Hi Product Hunt! I’m Philippe, the creator and maintainer of LUFScale. LUFScale is a free, open-source desktop app for macOS and Windows that analyzes perceived loudness and normalizes audio to a chosen LUFS target with True Peak control. It supports MP3, FLAC, WAV, AIFF, M4A, OGG and Opus, offers before-and-after comparison, ReplayGain metadata and CSV reports, and never modifies or moves the original files.

projects.title: Show HN: Hush – Brown noise and a speech blocker in the macOS menu bar
projects.author: oldmanrahul
projects.summary: A MacOS menu bar app for brown/speech blocker noise. I've been using online "white noise" generators for over a decade because I find they reliably help me get in the zone for an hour or two of work. I didn't like the context switching cost of needing to find the active browser tab, so I created a mac menu bar app that makes it almost frictionless to enable/disable brown noise. How to try it: See releases zip on the GH repo. It's macOS 13+, notarized. Technical details: - brown noise via leaky integration - a low-pass, speech blocker via pink noise through a 10-band EQ - all synthesized in real time via AVAudioEngine There's also a pay-what-you-want page on Gumroad: https://rahulp6.gumroad.com/l/hush Always open to feedback or comments if this helps you in any way. TY!

projects.title: CopyClipOSS
projects.summary: Menu bar clipboard history for macOS. Encrypted at rest and locked behind Touch ID.

projects.title: Kodo
projects.summary: Kodo is a lightweight, modular IDE for Windows, with Linux support in the works. Itskox extension system lets you add syntax highlighting, themes, plugins, and smart editing features without bloating the core. Kodo includes Build & Run, an integrated terminal, Project Search, customizable shortcuts, and Insight code completion. Open source under GPL-v3.0, Kodo is developed by SS-YYC and KerbalMissile.

projects.title: 猫在｜把真实的它，带回桌面

projects.title: TetherShot

No account. No upload. No AirPlay hacks. Why bookmark it: • iPhone USB + Wi‑Fi + Android ADB in one app • Pixel-perfect — actual device frame, not a mirror • Menu bar + global hotkey from any app • 100% local. Zero telemetry. MIT open source • Homebrew, signed DMG, or npm For devs and creators who screenshot phones daily.

projects.title: OmniDock
projects.summary: One Mac app for the little shortcuts you use all day. Preview windows from the Dock, click a Dock icon again to hide its app, snap windows into place, and find what you copied earlier. App hotkeys, Finder actions, and menu bar controls are built in too. Moving from Windows? Keep familiar window habits without juggling separate utilities. Free and open source. No account needed; optional clipboard history stays on your Mac. macOS 12.3+, Apple silicon and Intel.

projects.title: Bloop
projects.summary: Bloop turns system audio or mic input into eight real-time shader skins - every frame reacts to what's actually playing. Keep it beside your work in the resizable Mini Player or send it to the menu bar. Drop in an MP3 playlist and export the whole thing as a finished video. Apple Silicon, notarized, no subscription. Two skins are free forever, and they're the full app, not a trial.

projects.title: Codex Usage
projects.summary: See every Codex usage limit, reset time, pace, and banked reset from your Mac menu bar. Pressure Check shows which limit you’re using faster than an even pace. Includes a local dashboard and CLI, with no signup or third-party backend.

projects.title: Sidq
projects.summary: You spend an hour getting Claude to understand your project. Then you open ChatGPT and start over from zero. Again. Sidq reads the conversations your AI assistants already write to your own Mac and carries the whole thing into whichever one you open next. One shortcut. Nothing is uploaded, nothing leaves your machine it works with the wifi off. Reads Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor and more. Native Mac app, written in Rust, notarized by Apple. Free to start.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】DeepDeck：支持 WebMCP 和网页工具生成的 Harness 桌面客户端
projects.author: jo32

github.name: jo32/DeepDeck
github.description: DeepDeck — an extensible desktop workspace for DeepSeek Harness.

projects.summary: 我做了 DeepDeck，一个基于 DeepSeek Harness 的开源桌面客户端，当前提供 Apple Silicon 和 Intel Mac 安装包，采用 MIT 协议。 它内置了一个支持 WebMCP 的浏览器：Agent 可以发现并调用网站提供的工具。对于尚未提供工具的网站，用户描述任务，Builder 会尝试网页操作、检查结果，并将可行的操作保存成可复用工具。 例如，在 X 上构建搜索、读取帖子、编辑和检查草稿的工具后，后续任务可以直接调用。工具源码和版本保存在本地，支持查看、禁用和回退；网站发生变化时，需要重新验证或修改工具。生成工具与网站原生工具分别标明来源。 首次构建工具需要额外探索和验证，节省的时间与 token 取决于后续任务，尚未发布量化对比。 项目源码 中文介绍与演示截图 下载最新版 Harness 社区中的完整介绍（中文在前，英文在后） 这是社区维护的非官方客户端。模型与凭据沿用 Harness 的配置。

projects.title: AI Coach
projects.summary: Hatch an egg, raise a desktop pet, and watch its looks and personality develop. AI Coach connects with Claude and shows its activity through your pet. Everyday tools unlock as it grows. For Mac, with your first egg included free.

projects.title: [开源推荐] Lyrimuse：一个智能匹配歌词的 macOS 桌面歌词工具（自荐）
projects.author: Yudaotor

github.name: Yudaotor/lyrimuse
github.description: Word-synced desktop lyrics on macOS for Apple Music, Spotify, QQ Music, NetEase Cloud Music, Kugou — and YouTube Music / Spotify Web in any browser. Actively maintained open-source LyricsX alternative. Floating overlay, Dynamic Island, menu bar or lyrics window; translation, romanization, Last.fm stats. | macOS 桌面歌词：逐字同步 · 翻译 · 粤拼 · LyricsX 替代

projects.summary: 一个常驻 macOS 菜单栏的桌面歌词工具。它同时向九个歌词源发起查询，把所有候选放在同一套标准下打分后再决定用哪份，避免现场版配上录音室歌词、粤语版配上国语歌词这类错配。除 Apple Music、Spotify 外，也能读取 QQ 音乐、网易云音乐、酷狗，以及浏览器里播放的网页版音乐。 亮点 歌词智能匹配，而且过程可查：九个源（网易云、QQ 音乐、酷狗、酷我、咪咕、Musixmatch、LRCLIB、LyricFind、AMLL）的全部候选统一打分——歌名/歌手/专辑吻合度、源上报时长与实际曲长的差、有没有逐字时间轴，Live/Remix/(Edit) 这类版本标记单独计分。每首歌都能点开看各候选得了多少分、赢家为什么赢，手动选定的会被锁定不被覆盖。同类项目多是「哪个源先返回就用哪个」。 国产播放器是一等公民：QQ 音乐、网易云、酷狗与 Apple Music、Spotify 同等支持，可多选；浏览器里的网页版音乐也能按页面进度条同步。 支持中文翻译、粤语粤拼、日语注音假名；翻译默认走 macOS 设备端翻译，歌词不出本机。 支持 Last.fm 记录播放，带本地听歌统计、榜单和全年热力图；没连账号也先记在本地，之后连上自动补传。 四种显示形态任意组合：桌面悬浮窗、贴着刘海的灵动岛胶囊、菜单栏歌词（可双排）、仿 Apple Music 的独立歌词窗口。 免费、GPL-3.0、无账号无遥测，Apple Silicon 与 Intel 都有构建。

projects.title: Show HN: Ditch; Build multiple products at once
projects.author: 0xmtn
projects.summary: Hey HN, I built Ditch because I'm running Codex across several projects and was losing track of what each agent was doing, which one needed me, and where I had left off. Plus, I have other work, so I'd like to leave my agents be and come back only when they need me, finish or fail. Ditch is a local desktop app for managing multiple Codex agents simultaneously. It keeps projects and sessions in one place, shows which sessions are active or waiting, notifies you when something needs attention, and makes it easier to move between projects without losing context. I’m also experimenting with remote control, shared context across agents, and higher-level orchestration, but I’m keeping this first release focused on the local Codex workflow in macOS. The Community Edition with its source code is at Github: https://github.com/DitchNow/Ditch I want to keep developing the local runtime as OSS so it can be extended and integrated into workflows beyond what I build into the official app. No account or email required. Just download the dmg and start adding your projects to the app. I’m especially interested in how other HN users organize multiple coding-agent sessions, what causes them to lose context, and which parts of the workflow still feel unnecessarily manual.

projects.title: Show HN: Slock – A one-bit messenger inside your capslock key
projects.author: jonaraphael
projects.summary: Two computers, one bit. Hi — I built slock, a small macOS menu bar app that connects two people through their capslock lights. Hold capslock on your Mac, and the other person’s capslock light turns on. Let go, and it turns off. That’s all. A tiny way to interact someone without opening a chat window. Invent a blink language, try Morse code, or just bother someone who agreed to install this with you. If you both opt in, the same key also becomes a push-to-talk walkie-talkie. It’s open source: simple Swift, end-to-end encrypted, no accounts, no analytics. While it’s running, capslock takes a break from capitalizing things. Pause it to get your old capslock back. Please enjoy this very elaborate way to blink a light. Thank you for checking out my little project!

projects.title: ScanCode
projects.summary: Scan QR codes and barcodes from your screen or camera, see exactly what they contain, and act on them - without leaving your Mac. One keyboard shortcut to scan your screen. Nothing gets uploaded. All processing happens locally. Open payment QR codes directly in your banking app, launch links, or build barcode-based automations.

projects.title: Capturo
projects.summary: A screenshot is a rectangle of pixels cut out of a bigger screen. No edges, no context, which is why one pasted into a slide always looks like it fell there by accident. Capturo fixes that in one pass: padding, background, rounded corners, shadow, window frame and output shape, set together and exported once. Paste straight from the clipboard. Runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded. Plus guides on how screenshots work per platform, in four languages.

projects.title: iWinBridge
projects.summary: iWinBridge moves clipboard text, links, photos, videos and files straight between your iPhone and Windows PC over the same Wi-Fi. Nothing is uploaded and no account is needed. Pair once with a QR code and they reconnect on their own.

projects.title: AutoShortFormVideoGenerator
projects.summary: AutoShortFormVideoGenerator is a desktop tool for turning long videos into short-form content that you can upload to YouTube or TikTok with an automated workflow. Unlike many cloud editing services, it's a one-time purchase. You can also keep your videos private because the program doesn’t require an internet connection, except when it needs to verify your license key. The best thing about the program is that it works for both human streamers and VTubers. Feel free to ask me any questions.

Designed for deep readers, researchers, and writers, it conditions screen light with 8 curated paper stocks, warm tinting, softened ink contrast, and microscopic paper grain. Includes customizable reading sliders, an instant shortcut and runs 100% offline with zero tracking.

projects.title: PDF Unlocker Pro
projects.summary: PDF Unlocker Pro is a secure, 100% offline desktop application for Windows that removes passwords and restrictions from PDF documents locally, keeping confidential files and bank statements completely private.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Keelhaven：macOS 菜单栏的 restic 备份工具
projects.author: shenxianpeng

github.name: shenxianpeng/keelhaven
github.description: Privacy-first macOS menu-bar backup app powered by restic

projects.summary: Keelhaven 是一个纯菜单栏的 macOS 备份应用，没有 Dock 图标，也没有主窗口。备份引擎是 restic，加密、去重、增量都交给它，Keelhaven 负责界面、定时和密码管理。 用起来是三步：选要保护的文件夹，选一个自己拥有的存储（外置硬盘、NAS/SFTP，或者任意 S3 协议的对象存储，比如 Backblaze B2、Wasabi、Cloudflare R2），再设一个定时（每小时/每天/每周）。设好之后它就在后台安静地跑，只有出错才弹通知。 仓库密码只存在 macOS 钥匙串里，不落盘、不写日志，也不会作为命令行参数传给 restic 子进程。写出来的是标准的 restic 仓库，哪天不用 Keelhaven 了，用 restic 命令行本身也能继续读取和恢复。 restic 需要访问任意目录、网络和 SSH，App Store 的沙盒放不下，所以目前只有 Homebrew 和一行 curl 脚本两种安装方式。还没有申请 Apple 开发者证书：Homebrew 安装会在安装时清掉隔离标记，能直接打开；如果是从网站下载 dmg 双击安装，首次需要手动允许一次。GPLv3 开源，界面支持中英文双语。 brew install --cask shenxianpeng/tap/keelhaven 如果没有 Homebrew 可以通过 curl 命令来安装 curl -fsSL | bash

projects.title: Kairo
projects.summary: Kairo reads any selected text aloud on your Mac from one shortcut, and summarizes, translates or humanizes it on your own OpenAI key.

projects.title: 〖独立工具推荐〗法脉：律师的本地离线法律库 + 法条笔记 + AI 合同审查（macOS）
projects.author: lttxzmj

projects.summary: 我是 SubnetDesk 的作者。SubnetDesk 是一个基于 RustDesk 独立维护的开源远程桌面项目，专门服务于“设备已经网络互通”的场景：同一局域网、可路由私网，或者通过 WireGuard、Tailscale、OpenVPN 等 VPN 连接的网络。 它去掉了公网设备 ID、信令、中继、云账号和代理等路径，改为直接连接 IP 地址或主机名；局域网内还可以通过 mDNS 自动发现设备。比较适合家庭实验室、办公室、教室和现场运维，希望把远程控制链路留在现有私有网络中的用户。 主要特点： 直接连接 IP 地址或主机名，TCP 端口可配置 mDNS 自动发现局域网设备，也支持手动输入地址 用户名和密码认证，密码以 Argon2id 哈希保存 首次连接核对并保存设备指纹，并支持 CIDR 来源网段白名单 保留远程控制、剪贴板、音频和文件传输等 RustDesk 核心体验 提供 Windows、macOS、Linux 和 Android 安装包 当前稳定版是 v1.3.0，采用 AGPL-3.0 许可证。需要说明的是，它不提供公网信令或中继能力，两台设备必须已经可以通过 LAN、私网路由或 VPN 互相访问。

projects.title: 做了个"每天待办"小工具：可以自定义每天要做的事，可以跳转 APP
projects.author: defiabell
projects.summary: 做了一个自己的 TODO 工具，这种工具很多，但是没有自己做的灵活可控。有啥点子都可以自己去实现。 简单说，这就是一个网站，在手机上可以将其放到桌面，使用上和 APP 没区别。 这个工具的特点是可以自定义跳转其他 APP ，例如我的待办是运动，我可以跳转 Bilibili 对应的视频。 在线用（公开实例，免费，不用部署，中英文）： https://yixi-app.pages.dev/today 截图： https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Defiabell/yixi/main/docs/images/today-paper.png 仓库（ MIT ）： https://github.com/Defiabell/yixi == 它长什么样 == 一屏上只放几件正在做的事。默认三件，可以改，我劝你别改多。因为每天最重要的事就那一两件。 每件事下面挂几条每天都要做的小事。比如「学英语」下面是「听读三遍」和「背 20 个词」，「健身」下面是「跟练 20 分钟」。这些不是一次性待办，是每天都要勾一遍的；勾完最后一条，这件事今天就自动算做了，卡片右上角的圆圈亮起来。 每张卡下面一排七个点，是过去七天。回看页能看到本周每件事做了几天、勾了几次。就这些。没有积分，没有连续打卡天数，没有提醒。 每条小事都能绑一个跳转。填的不是「 B 站」，是 bilibili://video/BV 号，按下去直接落在那个视频上；微信读书是某一本书，不背单词是某个词书，Keep 是某个课程，能给出 URL scheme 的 App 都行，https 链接也能填。 填的时候有个「试跳」按钮，App 真开了才算配好；不知道填什么可以按 App 名字查候选。填错了不会坏，只是跳到首页而已。 == 一些实在的 == 它是个网页，加到 iPhone 主屏幕就是一个不用安装的小 App 。勾选是即时反馈的，请求在后台走，断网了会退回整页刷新，不会出现半截状态。 存了什么：你写的目标和子任务、每天勾了哪几条。就这些。不放心公开实例就自己部署一份，Cloudflare Worker 加 D1 ，免费额度，十五分钟，代码同一份。 == 预判几个问题 == 「和 Things / 滴答清单比呢」——不比。那些是清单，能放一百条；这个故意只放几件，放不下的事就是今天不该想的事。 「为什么不做成 App 」网页加系统自带的能力够用，不用装、不用审核、不用订阅，改起来也快。 「安卓能用吗」页面是普通网页，安卓能开能勾；跳转靠 URL scheme ，安卓那边我没试过，欢迎试了告诉我。 「子任务每天都一样，不会腻吗」会。所以它没有连续天数、没有奖励，腻了就改，改完的那一刻它又只是一页纸。 欢迎试用

projects.summary: 桌面端的小窗功能 Catrace 管这些小窗的生命周期：谁来弹、弹在哪、点击按钮反馈。小窗里显示什么、能怎么交互，由插件决定，就像 VS Code 那样。 我的设想是：任何东西都可以写成插件，接入一个小窗窗口。 现在这个期待基本满足了——只需要写一个插件，就能在右下角玩德州。 我希望这块窗口是一块画布，任何人，甚至玩家，都可以在上面画画。 我觉得未来应该有些窗口，小窗就够了。先做出来看看，试试这种小窗交互的感觉，会不会是桌面的一种方向。这也是我这个项目的灵魂。 目前内置插件 久坐提醒：盯键鼠和前台软件，连续忙满一个工作窗口休息提醒。 定时提醒：喝水、护眼、固定时刻打卡，间隔或整点执行。 AI 编程助手：Claude Code、Codex 在终端里跑，小窗提醒进度和授权。 手机消息：短信和 App 通知弹到电脑上，验证码一键复制。 GitHub 动态：第一颗 star、第一个 issue，不用刷网页。 PasteDrop：直接将剪贴板里的图片，通过 ctrl+v 粘贴到桌面以及文件资源管理器。 统计图：今天坐了多久、这周哪天最狠，用来复盘。 全都是插件，插件中心随开随关。也可以自己写。

projects.title: Show HN: Petrichor – Native offline music player for macOS
projects.author: kushalpandya
projects.summary: Over a year ago I shared about Petrichor on HN[1] while it was still in alpha, it started out as a hobby for me and has now grown into a mature product while staying free and open source[2]. I've just released v1.7 that added a whole bunch of features that I originally envisioned for this app. It remains free and open source, doesn't do any usage tracking or analytics, and still strives to be one of the best music players available on the platform. Features: - Everything you'd expect from an offline music player! - Supports more than 40 audio file formats. - Map your music folders and browse your library in an organized view. - Stream Internet Radio and organize saved stations into collections. - Synced lyrics of a playing track when available, including ability to download missing lyrics. - Create, import or export playlists. - Smart playlists with conditional, negative, and regular-expression rules. - Manage the play queue interactively using drag and drop. - Browse music using folder view when needed. - Pin anything (almost!) to the sidebar for quick access to your favorite music. - Navigate easily: right-click a track to go to its album, artist, year, etc. - Native macOS integration with menubar and dock playback controls, plus dark mode support. - Miniplayer and immersive mode. - Gapless playback, Crossfade, ReplayGain volume normalization, Equalizer, Spatial Audio, and AirPlay 2 support. - Last.fm scrobbling support. - Shortcuts and Automation API support along with Siri. - Works well with large libraries containing thousands of songs. [1]: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44515266 [2]: https://github.com/kushalpandya/Petrichor

projects.title: Show HN: Sol, a fast, powerful music player for macOS, with Subsonic support
projects.author: fulltimefeline
projects.summary: Hello! You may have seen me post here before about my other app, Gramola, a music dock that slides out from the edge of your Mac's screen. Today, I wanted to showcase a sister project to it that I started building when I grew frustrated with other music players, when I was on the search for one to integrate Gramola with (their speed and their often outdated UI to be precise). So I made my own! Sol is a music player, podcasts and internet radio app for macOS that follows all modern macOS style decisions, while seeming familiar for fans of the good old days of iTunes. Here's some highlights: - Incredibly fast, even with hundreds of thousands of songs or more. - It browses the way you remember, and it's super customizable, with different views and ways to make it your own, from a multi-column browser, to a grid view, to having a spiritual successor to CoverFlow! - It supports multiple libraries, local ones, network storage, even Navidrome and Subsonic-compatible ones. Sol doesn't have a central library that everything you add gets added to, although you can set it up that way if you want, it simply keeps track of all the locations where you keep your music. - It plays a lot of formats, MP3, AAC, ALAC, FLAC, WAV, AIFF, Opus, Ogg Vorbis, DSD, Monkey's Audio, Musepack, AC3, EAC3, CAF, AU, W64... - Gapless playback, match sample rate mode, ReplayGain. - Cue sheets as virtual tracks. - Has a rich visual metadata editor. - 10 or 31 band equalizer. - 2 top bar visualizers. - Smart playlists. - LastFM integration, autoscrobbling and stats page. - Discord Rich Presence. - Automation and control via AppleScript, Shortcuts or Sol's own local API ( https://sol.fulltimefeline.com/api ) - Regex rules for metadata editing and folder importing. - A steered shuffle option called SolDJ. - Internet radio and podcasts. - Synced lyrics (and transcriptions for podcasts). - Metadata, lyrics, and album art fetching. - Absolutely ZERO telemetry or analytics. And more! Sol is predominantly Swift and SwiftUI+AppKit, and built on the robust foundation of SFBAudioEngine, forked to make it MAS-friendly. It's available on the Mac App Store free to try for 7 days, then it's just a $19.99 one time purchase. Hope you like it, feel free to ask any questions, technical or otherwise! https://sol.fulltimefeline.com

projects.title: Show HN: I built a version of Omarchy that runs on Apple Silicon
projects.author: martiano
projects.summary: I wanted to try out Omarchy before doing a full install, but I only have an M series MacBook so I would have to find a laptop and there's no official M support yet. So I decided to create something that allows people to test and run Omarchy on their devices so they can understand how it feels. So I built an app that allows you to run Omarchy Quattro as a native, hardware-accelerated app on your Apple Silicon Mac! It uses QEMU and Apple's HVF, a custom built Omarchy ARM image, a swift app enclosing it, and custom patches on Omarchy, QEMU, Hyprland and more. I tried many things, and this approach achieved the best results. The native keyboard experience with Super shortcuts works very well, along with all the rest. It supports any resolution (fixed ratio), retina or non retina displays, audio input / output devices, shared clipboard, and many other features. Since it runs on top of macOS, native features like universal clipboard and AirPods work smoothly. It takes ~3min to install, works the same as any other standard macOS app. The whole project is open source, so feel free it check it out on GitHub, install, PRs, etc.

projects.summary: 炼丹炉 Alchemy Furnace —— 让 Agent 不止会回答，也像一个正在与你共同生活的人 自荐一个正在开发的开源项目：炼丹炉 · Alchemy Furnace 很多 AI Agent 很能完成任务，但很难形成稳定、可辨认的表达习惯与相处方式。炼丹炉想探索的是：怎样让 Agent 不只是一张静态人设卡，而是能在对话中持续呈现性格、价值取向、知识偏好和情绪节奏的个体。 项目把这些语言模式和人格特质抽象成可组合的「金丹」：可以创建道人、让道人服用不同金丹，并观察它们在对话中如何协调、冲突与涌现。 主要能力 金丹炼制：把表达方式、思考习惯、技能倾向或人格特质沉淀成结构化配方；也支持从已有材料中智能蒸馏候选草稿。 道人塑造：为 Agent 配置身份、基础性格、头像、模型与所服金丹，形成可持续演化的对话角色。 人格融合：按权重和顺序组合多枚金丹，不只是拼接提示词，而是尝试生成新的行为规则与人格特征。 对谈与围炉论道：支持一对一持续对话，也支持多个道人围绕同一主题交流，直观看见不同人格之间的互动。 可追溯的演化过程：金丹、丹方版本、服用记录和融合来源均可追溯；金丹可以作为消耗品使用，并保留已吸收的能力记录。 本地优先桌面应用：基于 Wails，运行在 macOS 和 Windows 本机；数据默认保存在本地 SQLite，模型调用使用用户配置的 OpenAI 兼容接口，API Key 加密保存。 技术上，它由 Go 负责桌面端与业务编排，Python 负责语言模式合成与模型调用，Next.js 提供界面。当前提供 macOS Apple Silicon、macOS Intel 与 Windows x64 的桌面安装包。

projects.author: andreasmolnarde
projects.summary: I've been building Dashwise, an open-source "all-in-one" homelab dashboard for about a year. One thing that has always bothered me about homelab dashboards is configuration. Many of them look great, but setting everything up through large config files can become tedious. With Dashwise, I'm trying to make the dashboard itself easy to configure while also keeping integrations flexible. ## Built-in apps * *Shortcuts:* A Spotlight-like search for your homelab. Integrations can expose actions and shortcuts directly to the search bar. * *News:* Subscribe to RSS feeds and group multiple feeds together. * *Notifications:* Send notifications to Dashwise from Shoutrrr-compatible applications or through plain HTTP requests. * *Frame:* Turn the dashboard into a customizable smart display/screensaver. * *Links:* Store and organize bookmarks. This is still in an early prototyping phase. ## Integrations With many dashboards, creating an integration that feels truly native requires modifying the dashboard's code rather than adding plugins. Dashwise integrations are instead defined using YAML. They can fetch data from REST APIs and display it using reusable widget templates. An additional benefit of this approach is that the integration format is simple enough for LLMs to generate integrations fairly easily. ## Where it's going I'm planning to keep expanding the integration ecosystem and experiment with more ways for external tools to interact with Dashwise. For example, one thing I'm planning is a CLI that can report the progress of long-running commands and display it directly inside Dashwise. If you have any feature requests or feedback, let me know!

projects.title: Show HN: MaCcyP – coding agents push text to a clipboard manager's Agents view
projects.author: hstun
projects.summary: I recently forked https://github.com/p0deje/Maccy to make coding agents or even just regular old Claude Desktop work better with it. Coding agents are constantly writing text they expect you to copy and then paste somewhere else — a command for another terminal, JS for the browser console, SQL, a drafted reply. MaCcyP ("Maccy Put") is a fork of the Maccy clipboard manager where agents push that text into a separate Agents view in the maccy popup proactively so you don't have to hunt through conversations and fumble with copying, saving you time and errors (and maybe your wrists too!). For the question about why not just use regular maccy + letting agents pbcopy to your clipboard, that works pretty well but the agents can't be as proactive in putting stuff into your clipboard contents because it can just be too much noise. With this approach it's much more contained and enables some other nice features. Features: * Agents view beside your clipboard history. Each agent session gets its own conversation as a private space — the key it holds can't see, list, or touch any other conversation or see your regular clipboard history either. * Secrets masked on screen — whole items or just the marked spans; paste yields the real value * Runbooks arrive as one batch: an agent pushes a multi-step sequence in a single call — steps display in order, one notification instead of N, and each step is its own paste * Preview pane: select and copy just a fragment, or ⌘O any item into an editable scratchpad window (a scratch copy, never written back) * Syntax highlighting, multi-item runbook batches, opt-in notification banners with a Copy button * Local-only: a Unix socket inside the app sandbox, no network. Upstream Maccy's behavior is unchanged maccy-put skill (Claude Code): Teaches the agent to push proactively — the moment it writes destination-shaped text, without asking — and to announce it with a stable transcript marker (→ put in MaCcyP: …). Companion maccy-revise skill corrects items on request MCP server (bundled in the app): put / put_batch / list / get / update / delete, per-span sensitive marking, language hints — stdio, works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, anything that speaks MCP; a plain CLI covers harnesses that don't Install: notarized zip → drag to /Applications. Claude Code: claude plugin marketplace add harleensahni/MaCcyP, then claude plugin install maccyp@maccyp. https://github.com/harleensahni/MaCcyP — signed + notarized, macOS 14+. Built on the excellent Maccy by Alexey Rodionov, which I've been using for a long time. Even if you're not interested in maccyp, definitely checkout maccy.

projects.title: Show HN: Turn repeated coding-agent corrections into rules/skills

projects.summary: Hi HN, Peder here. My cofounder and I built Blume after coding agents ate our previous startup. While building our previous product we severely struggled with agent drift. Duplicated functions, incoherent architecture and sneaky production bugs. Worst being Fable, which writes such good looking code that you almost don’t notice deviant behaviour. We tried to enforce behaviour with all the best practices: rules, skills, docs, self-verification/testing etc. But they rotted faster than a human can maintain them, and using agents directly to maintain them just leads to bloat and more drift. So that is what we set out to solve. Blume is a desktop app that sits next to Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. It reads your agents' context setup (skills, rules, docs) and local session files. When you keep correcting the same things, blume proposes updates to your rules and skills as reviewable diffs. You approve or dismiss each one. To avoid bloat we extract intent, corrections, frustrations from agent sessions and group them into clusters. And when pain/recurrence thresholds are reached, only then an agent is sent to look for improvements. Analysis runs locally on your machine, using your local Claude Code or Codex harness. Your sessions/code are never sent to blume. It is free to use, with the only “cost” being limited token spend to extract signals and creating the improvements themselves. (We plan to monetise with optional cloud agents and team features going forward). The biggest gap in the product right now is that we don't yet measure whether an accepted change actually helped, in fewer corrections or fewer tokens spent re-explaining. We're working on that and think it's a core part of the product. Would love feedback, especially from anyone who's tried to keep agent rules/skills maintained across a team. Happy to answer anything about how it works.

projects.summary: 我是这个项目的作者，自荐一下。 现在的 AI 视频/图片创作大多是「网页抽卡」：提示词扔进网页会话，等结果、碰运气，素材散落在各家平台的对话框里，想拼成片子还得再拷去剪辑软件。做短剧、广告这类要批量出内容的活儿，这套流程撑不住。 AI Art Engine 想把 AI 创作变成工程化生产：一个本地优先的桌面应用（Windows / macOS / Linux，GPL-3.0），工程、素材、模型配置全部留在本地，项目本身不设任何服务端。创作流程用节点图组织——文本、图片、视频、声音、3D 模型都是画布上的节点，连线即流水线，批量任务排队执行，共同上游自动复用，最后在内置成片时间线上编排导出（ffmpeg 合成 MP4）。 几个我认为有意思的点： 短剧 Agent 流水线：单集剧本进去，Agent 依次完成节拍拆解、9 宫格分镜、4 宫格动态分镜（36 格），每一级产物都经过「导演审核」节点打分（PASS/FAIL，失败原因自动写入状态文件，重跑时自动带上），最终产出 36 条动态分镜视频。 3D 导演台：文生/图生 3D 模型（Meshy、Tripo、Rodin、Luma AI、Lux3D）连进节点即入 3D 舞台；也能丢参考图让 AI 用基础几何体搭出整座场景白模，摆机位、截站位图锁定构图，再喂给图生视频。 一键工作流：12 个行业模板（短剧分镜、游戏买量、电商带货、漫画出版、知识口播等），选模板 → 预览拓扑 → 落盘成宿主资产，也可以用自然语言让 AI 现场规划一张节点图。 不绑厂商：OpenAI、DeepSeek、智谱、Kimi、Google、可灵、MiniMax、火山方舟、ComfyUI 等 20+ 提供商，也支持 Ollama / vLLM / LM Studio 纯本地推理；模型 API Key 需自备（本地模型除外）。

projects.title: Show HN: The AI agent that works inside the apps you use
projects.author: mej2020
projects.summary: I'm Mitchell, the founder at Lava. The short version: it's a desktop app that puts an agent next to the apps you're already logged in to, and it does the work through a direct connection to each app instead of driving a browser. You describe a task, it reads your real data, builds a plan, and executes it. Scoped permissions: reads run freely, but writes, sends, deletes, and payments need your approval. A concrete one: you say "follow up with everyone from last week's demos" and it reads your CRM and your calendar, drafts the emails in Gmail, and posts the summary in Slack. That's one conversation, not four tabs. There are 200+ providers connected today, covering all the apps your team already uses, so the same shape works for whatever your stack actually is. Why a direct connection and not browser automation: we started with a browser agent and it was miserable. Every time a site updated its layout, something broke. It was slow, and there was no clean way to tell the user what was about to happen. A direct connection to each app means every step is a specific action with known inputs, which is what makes the approval screen possible at all. The tradeoff: we only support what an app makes available through its connection, and we had to build a connector per app instead of getting everything for free. What makes this different from the alternatives: you don't need an engineering team to set up a workflow. You describe what you want in plain language and the agent plans and executes it. You can switch between AI models, so you're not locked into one provider. For apps that don't have a connector yet, Lava can also work through your open browser tabs, so the agent isn't limited to what has a connector. And any conversation can become a scheduled routine that runs on its own. To be clear: the download is free, but the agent runs on credits or a subscription. You need an account for the agent to work. The part I'd most like feedback on is the permission model. Permission fatigue is a real problem and there's been a lot of discussion on HN about it. We use scoped permissions with three modes: always ask, ask before sending (the default: reads run freely, anything that writes, sends, deletes or pays stops and asks), and never ask. The default is the safe one and also the annoying one. The approval gate is also what stops a prompt-injected agent from doing something you didn't ask for. If every write needs your sign-off, the attack surface shrinks. Scheduled routines run without a prompt because nobody is there to answer, and I'm not fully comfortable with that asymmetry. If you've shipped something in this shape, I'd like to hear where you landed. Practical notes: direct download for macOS and Windows. The build is signed and notarized. Happy to trade notes with anyone building agents that touch real user accounts.

projects.title: Show HN: SubSmith – Turn your own videos into language-learning material
projects.author: IbrahimF96
projects.summary: I've been learning Japanese for a few years and kept running into a similar problem. I'd find a video I wanted to learn from, hear a useful sentence, and then realise that turning that sentence into something I could study later was both time consuming and draining at times. I would end up jumping between a video player, subtitles/transcription, a dictionary, screenshots, audio clips and Anki. So I built SubSmith to bring that workflow together. You can drop a video or audio file into it, generate a transcript locally and then use the transcript alongside the media to: * look up words and sentences * replay individual lines * edit the transcript * save useful sentences with their original context/audio * export them as Anki cards The important part for me is that it works with your own media. It isn't tied to a particular streaming service or library, so I can use the random anime episode, podcast, lecture, etc. that I'm actually interested in studying. It's an offline-first desktop app, and transcription happens locally rather than sending the media to a transcription API. I'm sharing it here because I'm now more interested in finding out where this workflow breaks down for other people rather than adding features randomly now that I have solid core/base. For example: * Would you actually save sentences from your own media? * Which part of this process feels like too much work? * Does having the audio/context attached make creating an Anki card more useful? * Would you prefer this to work inside your existing video player/browser? * Is installing a desktop app a significant barrier? * And does requiring an account before starting the free trial make you give up? The current version does require an account to start the trial, and I'm trying to work out whether that's meaningful friction for the people who would actually use this. It's free to try, and I'd particularly appreciate feedback from people who already learn languages through their own videos, anime, films, podcasts or other media. projects.title: 【开源自荐】Clean My Codex：查看和清理 Codex 占用的磁盘空间
projects.author: FinnaXxx
projects.summary: Clean My Codex 是一款开源桌面工具，用来查看 Codex 在本机占用了多少磁盘空间，以及这些空间分别被什么占用。它也把会话、会话资产、Worktree、工作区和插件放到一个界面里管理。扫描和清理都在本机完成，不会上传会话内容或文件元数据。 为什么做这个 用 Codex 久了，本机会慢慢积累不少文件：会话记录、为任务创建的 Worktree、Worktree 里的依赖和构建产物、生成的图片与可视化、Plan、插件旧版本，以及安装或更新中断后留下的临时目录。 这些文件分散在不同位置。只看 ~/.codex 的总大小，很难知道磁盘空间用到了哪里；直接进目录手动删除，也可能漏掉会话的数据库记录，或者让 Git 留下失效的 Worktree 记录。Clean My Codex 就是为了解决这个问题，把扫描、查看和删除放到一个界面里。 支持的功能 扫描 Codex 数据目录、会话、会话资产、插件、Worktree 和工作区，并按类别显示文件数量与磁盘占用。 统一管理未归档和已归档会话。一个会话即使有多个续写文件或多层子代理，也会合并成一项；删除时会一并清理关联资产、索引和数据库记录。 单独查看和删除会话资产，包括 ImageGen 生成的图片、Visualization 及其查看器、Plan 文档，并显示来源会话、文件数量和占用。 查看 Codex 创建的 Worktree、Git 状态、构建产物占比和关联会话。删除时使用 git worktree remove；用户自己创建的 Worktree 只统计，不提供删除。 查看 Codex 在用户文档目录中创建的工作区，标出未提交、未推送或状态未知的 Git 仓库，避免误删仍在使用的文件。 管理插件版本，区分当前版本、旧版本和卸载残留；还可以设置定时清理，定期处理确认安全的临时目录、插件旧版本和过期会话。 只有存在明确证据时，项目才会进入“建议清理”。配置、凭据、运行期数据库、桌面端登录数据和缓存等内容会计入总占用，但不提供删除；当前插件只通过 Codex 自己的卸载接口处理，不会被当成普通目录直接删除。 支持平台 macOS 12 及以上，提供 Apple Silicon 和 Intel 安装包。 Windows 10 及以上，目前提供 x64 安装包，属于实验性支持。 安装与提醒 可以从 GitHub Releases 下载。项目使用 MIT 许可证。 目前仍在测试阶段，清理属于永久删除。第一次使用前建议先备份 Codex 数据，并在清理前退出 ChatGPT/Codex。macOS 安装包尚未公证，Windows 安装程序也还没有签名，首次打开时可能需要手动确认。

projects.title: Show HN: WhisperBar Trying to Fix Both Reading and Writing in the AI Age
projects.author: ne01
projects.summary: I am excited to share WhisperBar with fellow developers or anyone who reads & writes a ton of text when interacting with their AI agent. For the writing part, WhisperBar does what all other Whisper* apps do but a bit faster and more consistent, with a nice, stable, native macOS and iOS app. But where it really shines is in solving a problem that I'm sure you have encountered too: because of AI, we now have to read and comprehend so much more than before. Text to voice systems are not available everywhere, but even when they are, they sound so mechanical, and listening to the entire output is even more time consuming. What Gemini did by turning your research/response into a podcast was genius, and ChatGPT's new voice chat system is also much better (it allows you to have a conversation with the response). However, these two are not available everywhere that I interact with AI (specially with Claude Code and Codex) With WhisperBar, I can select a piece of text (anywhere, in any app) and press my keyboard shortcut to quickly listen to a short, ~20-second explanation. It does not matter how long the text I have copied is. This allows me to copy the entire response and then hear a summary, or select a section to zoom in on an explanation of that section of the document. Again, the point is that it is not text to voice, rather, it processes the text and comes up with a natural sounding short explanation. Oh, and another thing we don't store any data and only use providers with zero-data-retention policies. It is still a work in progress, and we have about 20 customers right now. It is available on the App Store for both iOS and macOS, with a 7-day free trial at only $4/month (plus Family Sharing). FYI, the WhisperBar iOS app is a bit different (it can record in the background for meetings, etc.). Let me know what you think :)

projects.title: Show HN: Open Session, the open-source cloud agent-orchestrator
projects.author: 9ranty
projects.summary: Open Session is an open-source cloud-based agent orchestrator. Self-host and use it with any model you like (or all of them). Open Session started as an internal app at Tella (YC S20). It’s become our most important tool. The whole team uses it, and not just for product development. It’s also great for customer support, operations, and data analysis. In the last couple months we turned it into something that other teams might want to use and adapt. When we started working on it earlier this year, our main frustrations with existing tools were (1) the lack of adaptability, (2) lack of good cloud-based workflows, (3) price (e.g. on Devin you couldn’t use your existing Claude sub). Open Session solves all three of these things for us: It’s open-source, so you can do what you want with it. But it also has extensibility built into the product. You can connect MCPs, skills, integrations, sandbox providers and more. Our team relies heavily on its Slack, Plain and GitHub integrations. It’s designed to run on your cloud (Mac mini also works). So you can close your laptop, run as many agents as your server can handle, and code from your phone. We’ve also made it easy to work together with your team. You can share a session with others as a link. They can steer the agent in the same session with you, or start a related session in a new tab. It’s self-hosted, so you only need to pay for your servers and the token costs. It also has some nice tools for managing AI subscriptions across your team. You can use Open Session in your browser or as a desktop app. You can also use it on your phone with the iOS app (coming soon) or PWA. Yes, we know everyone is building a harness right now. But so much is changing about how we build software and the best way to figure out where it’s all headed is to help decide the direction yourself. We hope your team enjoys using Open Session as much as ours.

projects.title: Show HN: Hostflip – a macOS /etc/hosts switcher that detects external edits
projects.author: heroncoder
projects.summary: Hi HN — I built hostflip, a native macOS menu bar app for switching /etc/hosts profiles. It is free and open source under the MIT license. The problem I wanted to solve was not just editing hosts entries. It was sharing /etc/hosts with Docker Desktop, VPN clients, scripts, and manual edits without one writer silently erasing another's changes. On first run, hostflip captures a read-only baseline (called Base Hosts) from the existing file and keeps the untouched original as hosts.orig. Active profiles are appended after the baseline in a clearly marked block. Writes are still atomic whole-file replacements under the hood. Before each write, the daemon hashes the live file and compares it with the expected hash. If they differ, it refuses the write; the app shows a diff and asks the user to reconcile the change first. A few other details: - Profiles can live in groups. At most one profile per group is active, while active profiles from different groups and standalone profiles stack together. - After a one-time approval in System Settings, subsequent switches no longer prompt for a password. The root helper is registered through SMAppService and exposes a single XPC operation: atomically replace the hosts file with merged content. The app and daemon verify each other's signing identity. - The bundled CLI shares the same workspace as the app and supports structured JSON output. hostflip doctor dev.example.com traces a hostname from profiles through the merged output and the live /etc/hosts file to the system resolver. - Remote profiles can refresh from HTTPS sources on a schedule. There is also an importer for existing SwitchHosts configurations. - The editor has cross-profile hostname/IP search, comment toggling, basic validation for malformed hosts lines, and stays responsive with large remote profiles. The app is built with Swift and SwiftUI, distributed through Homebrew or a signed and notarized DMG, and currently requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. Intel, Windows, and Linux are not supported. I would especially like feedback on the conservative drift behavior: if another process changes /etc/hosts, hostflip blocks further writes to the system file until the user reviews the diff. How do you handle multiple writers to the hosts file, and would you expect a different reconciliation model?

projects.title: [Open Source] MulmoTerminal: colour and sound show which AI agent needs you
projects.author: isamu

github.name: receptron/mulmoterminal
github.description: Run multiple Claude Code and Codex sessions in parallel — a browser terminal grid that shows which agent needs you. Local, tmux-backed, MIT.

projects.summary: Project URL Category JS Project Title Colour and sound show which AI agent needs you Project Description Run Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok, Muse and plain shells side by side in one browser grid. Colour plus a per-event sound means the session waiting on YOU is the one you notice, not the one printing the most. Local, tmux-backed. Highlights 1. It drives the CLI you already installed, rather than replacing it. MulmoTerminal is not an agent and has no model of its own: it starts the claude, codex, agy, grok or muse binary you already have, with your existing login and your existing subscription. There is no account to make, no API key to paste, and no proxy in the middle — the conversation goes from your machine to the vendor exactly as it does when you run the CLI by hand. 2. Colour AND sound, from the agent's own hooks rather than from watching its output. Claude Code emits PreToolUse, Stop and Notification; MulmoTerminal reads those and shows working / needs you / done as three different colours. This matters because the two states that cost you the most look identical in a terminal: a session blocked on a permission prompt and a session still thinking have both simply stopped printing. Scraping the scrollback cannot tell them apart; the hook can. (Codex does not report blocked-on-input — its approval prompt is drawn in its TUI and never reaches the rollout file — so for Codex the grid shows working / done only. The tool says so rather than pretending otherwise.) 3. Sound is the half that works when you are not looking at the screen. Colour only helps the eye that is already on the grid, which is exactly the eye you do not have when you are reading code in another window. So there are seven separate moments that can ring, and each one can carry its own sound file: finished (the turn ended), waiting (blocked on input), command-done / command-failed (a Run cell's exit code), session-exited (a PTY ended), worker-failed (a hidden background worker died — the only kind raised for a session with no cell on screen), and pr-ci-failed (a directory's PR went red). Give waiting one chime and finished another and you stop looking at the grid at all: you learn the difference between "come now" and "when you get a moment" by ear. Two of them — finished and waiting — also go to your phone as a Web Push, so the grid does not have to be open anywhere. 4. Real PTYs behind tmux, so closing the browser is not closing the work. Every cell is a real pseudo-terminal in a tmux session. Close the tab, reboot the browser, come back — the sessions are still there with their scrollback. Because the UI is a web page rather than a desktop app, the same URL on your phone over the LAN is the same grid: you can approve a prompt from the sofa without installing anything on the phone. 5. A cell does not have to be an agent. Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok and Muse all sit in the same grid, and so does a plain shell — so the place you watch your agents is also the place you run git log and npm test. Each cell can get its own git worktree, so several agents work on separate branches of one repository without stepping on each other. 6. MIT, and it starts in one command. npx mulmoterminal@latest — Node 22.12+, and at least one agent CLI already on your PATH. Nothing is uploaded, nothing is installed globally. Example Code bash Node 22.12+, with at least one agent CLI (claude / codex / agy / grok / muse) installed npx mulmoterminal@latest opens — up to 9 live sessions per page A repository can carry its own look in a .mulmoterminal.json at its root, so each project is recognisable at a glance in the grid. This is the one MulmoTerminal itself ships: json { "badgeColor": "#1a1d75", "headerColor": "#2c30a5", "headerTextColor": "#ffffff", "cellColor": "#f2f2fb", "cellBorderColor": "#5156d6", "dotColor": "#5156d6", "buttonColor": "#cfd0f7" } Screenshots or Demo Videos Guide (Japanese):

projects.title: Show HN: A skill for uploading full-resolution images to ChatGPT mobile runtime
projects.author: Byte-Naut
projects.summary: In work mode of the ChatGPT mobile app, if you upload a large image directly(even you choose "upload file" instead of image) for runtime processing, the image will always be highly compressed and many details would be lost. And if you choose to run it in the desktop app or pre-upload it to your imagebed to generate a url, it makes things complex-especially when you just want to extract things from some long screenshots by uploading, scripting automatically and getting the results smoothly in your phone. Tired of this, I try to build a skill that could be easily added into ChatGPT mobile apps that provides an origin-like lossless image upload experience. It works simply: every time a high-quality big image needs to be uploaded to the runtime losslessly, the session shows a temporary-imagebed upload url, you upload in the inner browser, get the url, and paste to ChatGPT to download to its runtime environment-if you have installed the Dropbox plugin it will preferentially use Dropbox for safer transfer, multiple transmissions at once, as well as no need to copy url mannually. Everything works to enhance ChatGPT image app upload, without compression, no need to switch apps, no need for cloud storage configuration. I'd like to listen to how you deal with questions like that, if there's a simple way to achieve, or any feedback to the skill itself. The skill is open-source: https://github.com/Byte-Naut/send-lossless-images-skill

Overtime we added image nodes, notes, terminals, coding editors, source control, etc. I wasn't sure about it at first. It took me a month to give the first version Souren built a real try. What got me was an Apple System Update I've been ignoring for weeks to avoid losing my +20 open claude code tabs in warp. In the course of using it and contributing, I broke it a few times and had to go back to the way we were doing things. It was miserable. It's been a few months now and I can't imagine going back. Most of you are builders and this tool should be really helpful. So I'd love for you to give it a spin. I would love your honest opinion. For the rest of the discussion, I would love to focus on the question of what is the right UI for agentic engineering? I would argue IDE is too much in the way, TUI is a terrible DX with a lot of hacks just for basic features. Finally, a GUI chat interface is far better but lacks the dimension of seeing the connection between items and is a poor collaboration surface. Now infinite canvas has a sprawl problem too, What do you think?

projects.title: Show HN: Trace – Offline Mac meeting transcription, overhauled from HN feedback
projects.author: AG342
projects.summary: A couple of months ago I posted about Trace, a non-intrusive, shortcut-driven Mac app that records and transcribes your meetings on-device. I know, another meeting transcription app, but we've had a great response and I'm confident it fills a niche. Here's the original post: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48521236 We've been working hard to bring community feedback on board, and the app is now so much more capable that it deserved a new post. Trace is still a minimal, out-of-the-way alternative to MacWhisper, but it's grown a lot of features since then, and the vast majority came from suggestions in the original HN thread. The biggest additions, to me, are below (full list here: https://traceapp.info/changelog ). - Trace used to live entirely in the menu bar and push everything out through the clipboard. It now has a History window to read, search, replay and manage every transcript in one place. From there you can correct transcription errors, label speakers and export to other apps. - Trace is now meeting-aware. When an app starts using the microphone, it prompts you to record, and you can teach it to auto-record on a per-app basis. It also offers to stop once the microphone is released, which was one of the most common requests (people kept forgetting to stop a recording when they'd hidden the pill). - There's a new in-person mode, so a meeting held in the same room is picked up through the mic and split correctly by speaker rather than coming out as one long monologue. - Speaker memory now persists between calls, so Trace can suggest names for voices it recognises. This massively speeds up naming participants. - Alongside marking key moments, you can now grab screenshots. Trace runs OCR on the capture and saves the text with the transcript, so it's searchable. - On-device summaries give you a short recap of the meeting, generated by a local model (Qwen by default, though you can switch it out or point Trace at your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint). - If you're about to join a call with people you've met before, Trace briefs you on what you discussed last time to get you up to speed. - Trace now detects the meeting language, so the live recap can translate in real time, and it handles non-English languages far better than before. - External audio and video files can now be imported and transcribed. - There's a separate tracecli tool for driving Trace from the command line. It includes "tracecli transcript --live --follow", which streams an accurate transcript while the meeting is still running. I use this to let a local LLM follow along live with a meeting. We also included a few quality-of-life fixes raised in the original thread. Audio is now written to disk as you record, so a mid-meeting crash can't corrupt the recording, the echo cancellation algorithm has been rewritten and there's a direct download for people who can't or don't want to use the App Store. Based on feedback that Trace was priced too low, we've also reworked the licensing. It's still a one-time lifetime licence with lifetime updates and no upgrade fees, but it now starts at £29 for a single Mac, with multi-Mac options too. There's also a 7-day free trial, so you can put it through its paces on a week of real calls before committing. Feedback is very welcome.

projects.title: Show HN: RAM based Linux distribution Invelinux for low-end hardware, 1.0 Stable
projects.author: sumtas
projects.summary: Hi, I am sumtas! I want to present a pretty cool project to Hacker News that I have been working on for the last 8 months. It is an independent, initramfs based distribution tailored for older computers that might be going to the landfill. It has a collection of QoL features for power users who want to try this niche operating system on their hardware. 1. It saves system configurations (/etc), applications (/bin), user configurations (/usr) into an external drive with a partition named "INVEL_AMPS". These directories can be accessed from the /storage/AMPS directory. 2. To install applications on this persistent drive, Invelinux uses its custom made package manager called AMPS (Automatically Mounted Packaging System). Its syntax and commands are relatively straightforward for beginners since it is also coded in Bash. 3. The system keeps itself minimal with the Toybox userland and the musl C library, and its init system is like SysV inits. As init, systemd is avoided entirely. Invelinux uses Toybox's init with relatively easy to understand shell scripts, a user can add their own scripts inside the /etc/init.d/rc.d directory to manage their systems seamlessly. 4. Due to its minimalistic architecture, this distribution can run on almost any low-end hardware with an amd64 processor. 5. As a window manager (yes there is a window manager), Wayland's reference compositor Weston was chosen due to its lower dependency track and simple customizability using simple .ini scripts, although in the future Lua support could be added for further customization. As a senior year high school student, it isn't the easiest project to maintain and it certainly takes time. If you want to support this project's growth without donating anything, you can star our Codeberg repository or create an issue on a bug you might find while testing out the operating system. You can also just comment by giving feedback that would mean a lot to me and to this project. Thanks! - sumtas Codeberg Repo: https://codeberg.org/sumtas/invelinux Wiki/Handbook: https://sumtas.codeberg.page/wiki

projects.title: 【开源自荐】TreeClip：一键识别、批量复制网页同类文本
projects.author: bluishwu
projects.summary: 文档： Chrome商店： 自荐： 1. 项目的思路新颖，网页具有结构，故利用结构特征识别同类元素，批量提取其中文本。 2. 应用场景广泛：潜在场景有商品列表、搜索结果、文章目录、排行榜、下拉菜单和论坛帖子等。除批量复制外，还可快速统计同类元素的数量，例如通过批量选择帖子标题，查看论坛当前页面的帖子数。 3. 功能完整，项目成熟度较高：项目于 2025 年 4 月发布初版，近期完成了代码重构、性能优化、UI 与 Logo 升级，并上线官网及完整文档。目前支持点选、框选、同类选择、层级切换、层级绑定、块内字段提取、文本清理、输出格式设置及多种面板形态。 4. 前景广泛：网页结构复杂多样，同类元素识别的准确性和兼容性仍可持续改进。希望通过开源吸引更多用户和开发者参与，共同完善识别规则、适配更多网页场景。 感谢！ TreeClip 文本批量选择器 TreeClip 是一款网页文本批量选择工具。点选、框选文字，一键扩展同类文本，批量复制到剪贴板。 难以选中结构相似却排版混乱的网页文本？厌倦了逐条复制？想一次提取网页中分散或同类的文字？ TreeClip 提供了多种灵活的文本选择方式（同类选择、点选、框选），并结合层级切换、层级绑定、块内字段、自定义输出格式等功能，大幅提升您从网页复制信息的效率。网页表格、下拉菜单、商品列表、文章目录、排行榜……更多场景待您探索。 快速开始 1. 按住 Shift ，点击目标文字，或者按住鼠标左键拖出选框。 2. 选中一个文本块后按 F ，批量加入网页中结构相同的文字。 3. 按 Ctrl + C ，按照当前输出设置复制所有已选文本。 4. 按 Esc ，清除全部选择并退出选择模式。 基础选择 同类选择 选择一处文本，再按 F 快速选择页面中结构相同的内容。 适用场景： 复制结构相同、类型一致的内容，例如搜索结果、商品标价、贴文标题等。

projects.author: CqwqY
projects.summary: CAID-浏览器ai副驾 Chromium 扩展（MV3，Chrome + Edge 双发），零构建，不接管浏览器原生新标签页，在任意网页可唤出 AI 副驾；内置插件系统，侧边栏区块 / 主面板 / 弹窗，全部可由你手写 JavaScript 插件自由扩展。仓库地址 官网 副驾侧边栏形态 副驾底部栏形态 运行示例 项目特性： 不占用新标签页：保留浏览器原生新标签页，零侵入。右键点扩展图标 →「选项」即可打开工作台设置页。 跨页 AI 副驾：任意网页右下角浮球唤起副驾，MAIN world 运行、绕过页面脚本干扰；选中文本 → 右键 → 附带上文启动。支持 AI 回答 与 Bing 搜索 双模式、待办、长期记忆。 第六感 · 主动协助（测试版）：采集行为信号（停留、滚动、复制、搜索）在本地推断意图，弹一条轻量气泡建议，点击即唤醒副驾执行对应任务；内置 17 个场景 + 规则表化可扩展，触发场景逐项可开关。全程本机处理，不记录页面正文。 轻量插件系统：用 JavaScript 自制功能区块，零部署、代码存你自己浏览器本地。 服务器监控卡片：填一个可访问地址，零部署探测在线状态与响应速度。 数据本地化：设置、插件、副驾配置全部存于浏览器本地，不依赖任何后端。 长期记忆：副驾拥有长期记忆 安装说明： 1.进入发布链接： ，下载zip后解压 2.打开浏览器开发者模式 3.导入解压缩的拓展导入即可 使用 1.配置 双击展开面板，点击上方设置，打开api配置，输入自己的LLM的api 2.呼出 单击右下角圆球呼出输入栏，双击打开面板。发送信息给副驾即可，运行时会有急停按钮，快捷键 ctrl+L 状态解析： 蓝色小球：正常状态 绿色小球：运行中 红色小球：出错 黄色小球：运行完成 3.拓展界面 右击上方拓展图标进入拓展选项 或 鼠标悬浮于小球后点击产物页 插件，记录，以及拓展功能设置将会在此地显示 特色功能使用 AI错题本功能 往往ai容易犯错，总拿其没办法，现在你可以通过悬浮球向ai写错题本，ai将会在每次执行任务前查阅错题本，并遵守解决方案 AI第六感 在你长时间浏览网页或者你滑动深度深的话，插件会认为你对此感兴趣，可能会在上方悬浮提示你是否要继续看 或 当你在AI所记录的网页浏览，ai则会对当前场景做出建议 如：在电商网站，识别到电商元素或特定网站，将会询问是否需要总结 在github等代码平台，会询问是否需要代码分析等等 打扰？ 你可以进行屏蔽某些网站，甚至关闭智能推荐来，，免除打扰 已知问题 对于AI第六感，还在测试中，且目前使用的是代码逻辑判断，无法对所有网站进行建议 对于副驾，副驾的识别能力是从内（源代码）层面看网页，容易不认得一些图形化按钮，目前修复方法是识别css标签，但仍会有误 且操作由AI执行，一些模糊不清的语句容易使其摸不着头脑 License MIT

projects.title: 【开源自荐】以多行平铺的方式展示当前窗口所有标签页的chrome 扩展
projects.author: hezhizheng
projects.summary: Multi-Row Tabs（多行平铺标签栏） 一个 Chrome 浏览器扩展（Manifest V3），以多行平铺的方式展示当前窗口的所有标签页，采用零侵入浮动模式：不修改页面任何样式，兼容所有网站。github 视频演示 背景说明 Chrome 扩展无法修改浏览器原生标签栏（标签栏属于浏览器 UI 层，扩展无权注入样式或脚本）。因此本扩展采用「浮动覆盖栏」方案：页面上仅有一个可拖拽的悬浮按钮，点击或按快捷键时标签栏才浮现在页面顶部，不改动页面任何样式，对等任何网站零影响。 功能特性 零侵入浮动模式：标签栏默认隐藏，不修改页面任何样式；展开时浮在页面上方，鼠标离开自动收起 悬浮按钮可拖拽：右上角小圆点按钮可拖拽到页面任意位置，位置自动记忆 自定义快捷键：默认 Alt+Z，可在弹出面板中录制任意组合键，随时展开 / 收起标签栏 多行平铺展示：标签以 favicon + 标题的形式自动换行平铺，当前活动标签白底高亮 标签排序：标签栏左侧提供排序下拉框，支持「默认」（与浏览器标签顺序一致）、「按名称」（中文拼音排序）、「按域名」（优先按一级域名排序，同站点不同子域名的标签自动聚在一起），选择后自动记忆 一键切换 / 还原：点击工具栏图标，在弹出面板中一键显示或隐藏整个功能 标签操作： 左键点击标签 → 切换到该标签 中键点击标签 → 关闭该标签（与原生标签栏行为一致） 点击标签上的 × → 关闭该标签 键盘导航：展开后用 ← → ↑ ↓ 在标签间移动焦点（蓝色高亮），按 Enter 切换到对应标签页，按 Delete 关闭当前高亮标签，按 Esc 收起标签栏 可选显示链接：在弹出面板中勾选「显示链接」后，链接以小字显示在标签名称下方（默认不显示） 实时同步：标签的新建、关闭、切换、标题变化会自动刷新标签栏 无 Mixed Content 警告：favicon 由后台抓取并转为 data URL 下发，http 页面的图标在 https 页面中也不会触发混合内容警告 安装方法 1. 打开 chrome://extensions/ 2. 开启右上角「开发者模式」 3. 下载 最新压缩包 解压 4. 点击「加载已解压的扩展程序」，选择本目录（multi-row-tabs） 5. 工具栏出现扩展图标即安装成功

projects.title: 【开源自荐】TopicConsole：轻量跨平台的 Apache Pulsar 桌面客户端
projects.author: yanbo92
projects.summary: TopicConsole 是一个开源、跨平台的 Apache Pulsar 桌面客户端，适合开发者和运维人员浏览主题、检查消息、搜索历史消息，以及进行基础的生产和消费操作。 它采用本地桌面应用形态，直接连接 Pulsar，不需要部署 Docker、JVM 或云端控制台。 主要特点 单体桌面应用，安装包约 15 MB 支持 macOS、Windows 和 Linux 直接连接 Apache Pulsar Broker 支持浏览主题、订阅和分区信息 支持消息搜索、查看、生产和消费 Observer Mode 使用 Pulsar Reader 检查消息，不创建持久订阅 凭据和配置保存在本地 支持 Avro、JSON、字符串等常见消息格式 基于 Wails、Go、React 和 TypeScript 构建 为什么做这个项目 很多 Pulsar 管理工具依赖较重，或者需要额外部署 JVM、Docker 和服务端组件。TopicConsole 希望提供一个启动更快、依赖更少、适合本地使用的桌面工具，方便开发者快速检查 Pulsar 集群和消息流。 欢迎大家试用，也欢迎对功能和 Pulsar 使用场景提出建议。 项目采用 AGPL-3.0 开源协议。

projects.title: Show HN: Reverse-engineered a gaming mouse's HID protocol to bring it to Linux
projects.author: blakok4
projects.summary: I’ve been reverse-engineering the HID protocol of an Attack Shark X6 gaming mouse (no official Linux support) using Ghidra and USB captures, and building a native Linux desktop app around it in Go + Wails, with a React frontend. The protocol itself is fairly advanced. DPI, RGB lighting, polling rate and button remapping are all documented at the protocol level. The app currently only exposes DPI configuration though, the rest is reverse-engineered but not yet wired into the UI. One piece is still unsolved: the macro report isn’t captured yet, so there’s no macro editor. If you’ve done HID/USB reverse engineering before, I’d appreciate a hand there. There’s also plenty of non-reversing work: building out the RGB/polling/remap screens in the frontend, implementing what’s already known in the Go backend, or testing on other Attack Shark models (X3, R1, X11) that likely share the same dongle and protocol. Happy to answer questions about the protocol work or the architecture in the comments.

projects.title: Show HN: Proliferate- open-source, self-hostable Codex for any coding agent
projects.author: pablo24602
projects.summary: Hi HN- I'm Pablo, the founder of Proliferate (YC S25)! Proliferate ( https://github.com/proliferate-ai/proliferate ) is an open-source, self-hostable AI IDE that lets you work and automate tasks with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and Grok in one place. Here's a quick 2m demo of how we use Proliferate to build Proliferate: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tGNX0oaWmBY I started building Proliferate after my team onboarded to OpenAI Codex. Within days, we were using it for everything: using computer use instead of navigating websites ourselves, having Codex coordinate other agents, and setting up automations for recurring work. We really never needed to leave the desktop app to get work done. If my team’s experience is anything close to representative, a Codex-like app (a horizontal agent with a beautiful UI) is the main interface every company is going to use to get work done. That is perfectly in line with OpenAI’s mission to make Codex the everything app (see: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47796469 ). But as we started automating work closer to the core of the business, I wanted to work with agents from all the labs, including open-weight models, without becoming increasingly dependent on OpenAI. And that’s what Proliferate is for! It's the open-source, self-hostable Codex that preserves your optionality across agents and model providers while building toward Codex’s breadth. Today Proliferate supports: * Working with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and Grok with their native inference and configuration options, including Bedrock, Azure, and self hosted inference. * Inter-agent communication and management: a parent agent can spawn and communicate with another supported agent as a subagent (I personally like to have Fable delegate to Codex, with OpenCode models reviewing PRs). * Building workflows- one of the features I'm most excited about. These are re-usable chains of agent sessions and human approval gates, with the harness and model chosen per step and documents passed between them. I use this to automate code review, QA, and my PR construction process. All of Proliferate is 100% open source under AGPL-3.0. There are still definitely some rough spots, but we’re building fast and I’d really love any feedback!
